newsitem.title: USA: Olsten results hurt by low-margin accounts.
newsitem.headline: Olsten results hurt by low-margin accounts.

text.p: Health care and information services provider Olsten Corp. Thursday reported lower earnings due to an increasing number of longer-term, higher-volume, lower-margin corporate accounts.
For the fourth quarter, Olsten earned $16.5 million, or 21 cents a share, compared with $25.3 million, or 33 cents a share a year earlier.
Revenues rose to $930.9 million from $738.6 million.

"As we anticipated and announced in November, our fourth quarter results were affected by margin pressures in both our Staffing Services and Health Services businesses due to a number of challenges," said Olsten Chairman Frank Liguori.
He said economic growth and low unemployment "should provide an environment for gradual margin improvement."
For the year, Olsten earned $54.6 million, or 70 cents a share, compared with $90.3 million, or $1.18 a share in 1995.
Revenues were $3.38 billion, up from $2.81 billion in 1995.
Olsten stock was up 50 cents at $18 in morning trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
